chunks: And Ali ibn Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-A'lawi narrated from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Ahmad ibn Abi Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Hassaan, from Abdurrahman ibn Kathir, who said:

One day I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and Muhzim al-Asadi was with him. He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, when is this matter that we are waiting for? It has been delayed too long for us.' He (peace be upon him) responded: 'O Muhzim, the wishful thinkers have lied, the hasteners will perish, the Muslims will be saved, and they will return to us.'

key_terms.الْمُتَمَنُّونَ: The wishful thinkers or those who make speculative claims about the timing
key_terms.الْمُسْتَعْجِلُونَ: The hasteners or those who rush ahead impatiently
key_terms.الْمُسْلِمُونَ: The true followers who patiently wait
key_terms.فِدَاكَ: May I be sacrificed for you (a term of high respect and devotion)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the three groups mentioned in the hadith regarding the waiting for the Imam's reappearance?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the nuanced Shia doctrine of *al-intizar* (waiting) during the Major Occultation, emphasizing that true salvation lies not in hasty speculation or premature claims of authority, but in patient fidelity to the Imam. The tripartite classification of *al-mutammunoon* (those who claim certainty prematurely), *al-mustajiloon* (the impatient), and *al-muslimoon* (the faithful who wait) underscores the scholarly emphasis on spiritual endurance and correct expectation. This hadith serves as a foundational text for understanding the psychological and theological posture of the Shia community during periods of political absence and occultation.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (8) Ali bin Ahmad narrated from Obaydillah bin Musa al-Alawi from Muhammad bin Musa from Ahmad bin Abu Ahmad from Muhammad bin Ali from Ali bin Hassaan that Abdurrahman bin Kuthayr had said:

One day I was with Abu Abdullah (as) and Muhzim al-Asadi was there too. Muhzim said, “May I be sacrificed for you! When will this matter, which you are waiting for, take place? It has been delayed too much.” He (as) responded: “O Muhzim, the ill-whishers have told lies, the hasteners will perish and the submitters will be saved and will be with us.”
